location: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, Key Largo
summary: A one-day marine science program for 115 students, organized into four cohorts rotating through three hands-on experiences at John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park.

rotation.heading: Four Cohorts, One Coordinated Day
rotation.intro: Students will be divided into four cohorts of approximately 28–29 students. Cohorts rotate among the boat tour, citizen science and fish identification, lionfish programming, and staggered lunch periods. Activities run concurrently, so the schedule below shows where each cohort will be throughout the day.

departure.label: Departure
departure.note: The program ends at 2:30 PM. Optional activities after 2:30 PM are not part of this proposal.

notes: Your group arrives on three buses, and the program begins at 9:00 AM.
Short gaps between activities are transition time for moving between the marina, the picnic area, and program areas.

days.title: One Day on the Reef
days.theme: Four cohorts rotate through three hands-on experiences at John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, 9:00 AM to 2:30 PM.

blocks.title: Glass-Bottom Boat Tour
blocks.description: Students view living coral reef habitat and the fish that depend on it from a glass-bottom boat, with a REEF educator helping them connect what they see to how healthy reefs work.
blocks.studentBlurb: Ride a glass-bottom boat over a living coral reef and spot the fish and corals that live there.
blocks.familyBlurb: Students view living coral reef habitat and the fish that depend on it from a glass-bottom boat, guided by a REEF educator.

blocks.title: Citizen Science & Fish Identification
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF's volunteer divers and snorkelers identify fish and record what they see, then practice the same identification and survey skills used in REEF's Volunteer Fish Survey Project.
blocks.studentBlurb: Learn how scientists and volunteer divers identify fish, then practice being a citizen scientist yourself.
blocks.familyBlurb: Students learn how REEF's volunteer divers and snorkelers identify and count fish, then practice the same survey skills.

blocks.title: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection, looking at anatomy and adaptations and learning why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.
blocks.studentBlurb: Take a close look at a real lionfish, an invasive species, and find out why it's a problem for Florida reefs.
blocks.familyBlurb: Students take a guided look inside an invasive lionfish and learn why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.

blocks.title: Picnic Lunch
blocks.description: Each cohort has a scheduled picnic lunch at the park. Lunch is not provided, so students and chaperones should bring a packed lunch.

studentsWill: Observe living coral reef habitat and marine life from the glass-bottom boat.
Learn and practice the fish identification and survey methods REEF's citizen scientists use.
Investigate invasive lionfish anatomy and adaptations through a guided dissection.
Connect what they see to REEF's ongoing reef conservation and invasive-species work.
